item.title: Mikel Arteta provides injury update on Bukayo Saka while defender set for long-awaited return
item.description: Bukayo Saka looks set for another month on the sidelines -Credit:Alex Grimm/Getty Images Mikel Arteta has confirmed that both Bukayo Saka and Martín Zubimendi will miss Arsenal's Premier League match against Newcastle United. The Gunners travel to St James' Park on Saturday, with Arteta's side sitting five points clear at the top of the table. As they look to extend their impressive run of five consecutive league victories to six, they will be forced to do so without two of their most influential players. Saka continues to be sidelined with the injury he picked up against Bayern Munich, while Zubimendi sustained a knock while on international duty with Spain. Tom Brady linked with Chelsea investment after abrupt Birmingham City exit U.S. Soccer executive opens up on search for Mauricio Pochettino replacement -Credit:Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images Arteta confirmed on Friday that Saka would not require surgery, but the England winger is still facing around a month on the sidelines. He said via The Mirror : "Yeah, so we had another test; he's evolving really well, but it's going to be an eight-week injury, more or less. So I think he's four at the moment, so it's still a while for him to be back with the team. "Martin [Zubimendi] is [also] out. Unfortunately, he has a muscular problem in his hamstring. He wasn't too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scan shows that there is an injury there, and he's going to be out for a few weeks, I think." While both Saka and Zubimendi are ruled out, William Saliba looks set to return to the squad for the trip to Newcastle. The French defender has been absent with a back problem since the FIFA World Cup, but Arteta confirmed he is ready to be selected, saying: "He's ready. He's in good condition. We want to ramp up his minutes. He played actually two games, one behind closed doors and one more official [the Under-21s], and he did really well and he's in good condition." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Bruno Guimarães was also a topic of discussion, with the midfielder preparing to face the club he left in the summer. Arteta expects a warm reception for the Brazilian, while also confirming that international teammate Gabriel Magalhães returned in good shape following the break. He commented: "Yeah both Gabi and him [Guimarães] came back and the same as the others and they are in good condition and we need to nail the preparation and we know how difficult it is to play against Newcastle. I hope (he gets a good reception), I think he was one of the main players, and he came in a really important part."

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes decision ahead of Liverpool test
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes decision ahead of Liverpool test Bruno Fernandes to Remain Manchester United Captain Under Mauricio Pochettino Mauricio Pochettino has made his first significant call at Manchester United and there is no ambiguity around it. Bruno Fernandes remains club captain. That was the headline from Pochettino’s first media appearance after taking charge at Old Trafford, where he inherits a side in the Premier League relegation zone and a dressing room that has looked unstable for weeks. His first assignment is brutal enough, an away trip to Liverpool, and he arrives with one obvious fire to contain, the future and authority of Fernandes. Bruno Fernandes Role Confirmed The Portugal international has reportedly turned down two contract offers this season. His current deal expires at the end of the campaign, which means from January he can agree a pre-contract with an overseas club and walk away for nothing. For a player of his profile, that is a major issue. There has also been noise around his behaviour. Fernandes publicly questioned his former manager’s tactics after the 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. He was then dropped for the 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth, before returning for the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea after talks with Michael Carrick. Photo IMAGO Mauricio Pochettino Sets Immediate Tone Pochettino did what a new manager often has to do, remove uncertainty, at least publicly. “I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one,” he said. “Bruno is our captain and he’s a very important player, but all the player must feel they are important. “We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone.” Manchester United Contract Issue Still Open This does not settle the contract stand-off. Pochettino admitted there “would be time” to address Fernandes’ long-term future and avoided making any stronger guarantee beyond the armband. That is sensible. Manchester United need points, order and clarity. Pochettino has started with the easiest message to send. The harder part comes next, winning matches and convincing Fernandes that his future still belongs at Old Trafford.

item.description: Russian tennis player Daniil Medvedev in action against US' Frances Tiafoe during their men's singles match of the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, an international tennis match in Turin. Medvedev, the 2020 champion, saved two break points in the fifth game of the opening set and immediately broke Tiafoe to go 4-2 up before serving out to take it in 35 minutes. item.title: Giants Rookie Malachi Fields Proves He Is Ready For More Touches
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Malachi Fields is not acting like a rookie. Through nine games, the Giants third-round pick has recorded 350 yards and one touchdown by catching 22 of 38 targets. He has yet to drop a pass. This reliability stands out in an offense that often struggles to move the chains. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy says he is not surprised by the rookie’s steady play. The team traded up to get Fields in April, giving up picks in 2026 and 2027 to secure his spot at number 74 overall. Fields has become a key part of the passing attack behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely. He has 10 receptions for 185 yards over his last three games. His big gain came in the recent loss to Washington where he had three catches for 62 yards. The offense looks different now that J.J. McCarthy took over as the starter in Week 7. McCarthy has given Fields more chances to make plays in space. Coaches See High Ceiling Matt Nagy believes Fields has a long way to grow. “Not surprised at all with him,” said offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, according to Sports Illustrated . “You all have heard me talk about him all camp. His ceiling — when we have this conversation five years from now, you’re going to think about this question you’re asking me because he’s really good.” Nagy told reporters on Thursday that the rookie does everything right. He catches the ball, blocks for runners, and makes plays when needed. The coordinator thinks the rookie’s potential will keep getting higher. Nabers agrees with the high praise. He highlighted Fields’ ability to separate from defenders and track the ball in the air. “Yeah, I mean, just giving him the ball in space, I think he gets open pretty well. I think he has good feet for how tall he is, he runs fast, can track the ball well. He gets in and out of his breaks,” Nabers said, according to Sports Illustrated . The veteran receiver is happy to see the team give Fields more opportunities to find his rhythm. Teammates Trust Him in Coverage Isaiah Likely no longer views Fields as a typical first-year player. The tight end sees a teammate who understands how defenses work. “I don’t really look at Malachi as a rookie anymore. I look at him coming into his own,” Likely said, according to Giants Wire . He explained that when defenses focus on him and Nabers, Fields must win his one-on-one matchups. Likely feels the rookie has done a great job of winning whenever he is asked to. Fields knows his role in these situations. He understands that if he gets single coverage, the ball is likely coming his way. “But Malachi’s definitely honed in on knowing that if I get one-on-one coverage, ball is most likely going to me. So I’ve just got to make my play,” Likely said while describing the rookie’s mindset. This awareness helps the Giants offense keep moving even when the other team loads up against the top targets. item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor managed only 21 rushing yards on 11 carries during Thursday night’s 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans, according to RotoBaller NFL . The former Wisconsin Badger added six receiving yards on four catches while playing in a game where his team fell behind early and tried to catch up. According to RotoBaller, Taylor did not score double-digit PPR points in three of his four most recent games. The defensive front in Houston made it hard for Indianapolis to move the ball. Taylor gained just 14 yards on his first four attempts and did not find much room after that. His team entered catch-up mode in the second half, which changed how the offense ran the ball. Quarterback Daniel Jones was benched for backup Anthony Richardson Sr. as the game slipped away. Game Script Changed Everything When a team is down by a large score, running the ball becomes less useful. The Colts needed to pass the ball to score quickly, but the quarterback could not connect on long throws. RotoBaller noted that Taylor’s stability in the passing game is a plus, but it is also a double-edged sword because it stems from the quarterback’s inability to attack deep. Jones struggled to get anything going downfield, which kept the offense in short-yardage situations. This dynamic forced Taylor to be a primary target for short passes even when the run game was dead. The result was a player who was essentially phased out of the game plan as the second half wore on. The offense needed a spark, but the game script dictated a pace that did not favor the running back. Week 11 marked a rough stretch for the star back. This trend makes him much more dependent on the game script, especially for a rebuilding Colts squad. When the team is winning, he can carry the load. When the team is losing, his value drops fast because the offense shifts to passing. Texans Defense Holds the Line The Houston Texans defense did exactly what the Colts needed them to do. They stopped the run early and forced Indianapolis to abandon their ground game. Taylor’s 21 yards on 11 carries show a clear lack of room to run. He had four receptions on five targets, which shows he was still involved, but the yardage was minimal. The defense did not allow the Colts to control the clock or the pace of the game. David Montgomery, the Texans running back, returned from injury to help the offense. He completed a full practice session for three consecutive days leading up to the matchup. item.title: Driver Adjustments Shift Aim, Cost Strokes For Amateurs
item.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Many golfers believe fixing their driver requires complex swing changes or expensive new equipment. A recent analysis shows that setup adjustments often yield better results than mechanical overhauls. PGA Tour putting coach Stephen Sweeney identified specific alignment issues that cause players to miss targets consistently. These errors start before the club even moves. The focus shifts from what is in the bag to how the body aligns with the ball. Stephen Sweeney broke down two critical errors that ruin short-game performance. The first mistake involves eye position relative to the ball. “Where your eyes are right now, I tend to see if players’ eyes are inside the ball line; they tend to look out to the right,” Sweeney said. The arrangement forces the putter to travel from inside to out, creating a path that works for full swings but hinders short putts. The fix requires hinging at the waist more to reach a “tabletop” position. Golfers should keep two putter heads of space from the ball to the toe line and bend forward until eyes sit directly over the golf ball. The second error involves a right-aligned putter face at address. Because the eyes were looking from the inside, the writer subconsciously aimed the face right and tried to pull the ball back to the line. Once the eyes moved on top of the ball, lining up the face became much easier. Sweeney showed a clever trick using a phone to check the aim. “Just go ahead and set up and aim your putter face,” Sweeney said. “If I go ahead and set the back of my phone to your putter face, and you come back and look down that line, you can see the face aimed on the right edge.” This visual confirmation helps players understand their true alignment versus their perceived alignment. Correcting these issues changes the entire stroke mechanics. Confidence returned, and more putts dropped after the writer made these two adjustments. Sweeney explained the mechanics clearly: “As the putter goes back, the putter is moving a little on the inside — but pretty square to where you aimed it.” Equipment like the TaylorMade Qi4D driver or Ping irons listed in Golf Monthly reports can enhance performance, but they cannot fix a broken setup. A player might have the best driver in the world, yet if their eyes are inside the line, the ball will miss the target. The relationship between setup and result remains the most consistent factor in golf. The Impact of Alignment on Scoring Alignment errors often go unnoticed because they feel natural to the player. Sweeney’s observations highlight how a small tilt in the eyes changes the entire path of the club. When eyes sit inside the ball, the brain compensates by aiming the face right. item.title: The most important stat was actually injuries in Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw with FC Köln
item.description: (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich’s 1–1 draw with 1. FC Köln was a pretty remarkable statistical contradiction. Vincent Kompany’s side controlled practically every aspect o f possession, but the numbers suggest that control did not translate into meaningful attacking superiority. Bayern finished with 71% possession, completed 732 passes at a 92% accuracy rate, registered 17 shots, and won five corners without allowing Köln a single one. Bayern also recorded 35 touches in the opposition penalty area compared to Köln’s 22. By most conventional measures, Bayern dictated the match. Match stats pic.twitter.com/NlydmG3YhJ — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 20, 2026 However, the more important numbers tell a different story. Despite taking 10 more shots than Köln, Bayern managed just one effort on target. Bayern’s expected goals total was only 0.94, less than half of Köln’s 1.98. The visitors also generated five big chances compared to Bayern’s two. Even more frustratingly, Bayern missed two of its big chances, while Köln squandered four. Both teams had opportunities to take all three points, but neither could capitalize enough to secure the victory. Ultimately, Bayern’s problem was not a lack of possessio n or attacking activity. I t was an inability to turn territorial dominance into genuinely dangerous opportunities while allowing Köln to create considerably better chances with far less of the ball. When you factor in this stat, it tells a little more of the tale for the game: Injuries to Harry Kane and Michael Olise: 2 A 1–1 draw was the result, but the underlying numbers suggest Bayern Munich should have been much better. item.title: Blues’ Three Surprises Prove This Season Is No Fluke
item.description: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The St. Louis Blues started the 2026-27 season with a 10-9-2 record, a mark that suggests a team stuck in the middle of the pack. These are lucky breaks and genuine shifts in the team’s identity that could carry them through a long winter. The Goalie Who Stole the Job Joel Hofer has taken the starting net and refused to let go. He is playing well and among the best in the entire league at stopping goals that should have gone in. MoneyPuck states that Hofer’s 8.2 Goals Saved Above expected ranks third in the NHL among goalies who have played 15 or more games. That number is wild for a team that often struggles to score. He has become the backbone of the franchise, and if his teammates can finally feed him the puck, he might get serious talk about the Vezina Trophy. A Waiver Wire Miracle Justin Barron arrived in St. Louis after being cut by the Nashville Predators. In just 19 games, he has scored four goals and added nine assists for 13 points. He also owns a stellar 55.36 expected Goals-For percentage, which shows he drives play better than almost anyone else on the blue line. A full season of this performance could give Barron a claim to being the greatest waiver claim in franchise history. As noted by Bleedin’ Blue , it would be wonderful for the Blues to possess their own version of “the Florida Panthers claimed Gustav Forsling” story. The team found a top-four defender for pennies on the dollar. The Rookie Who Filled the Void Adam Jiricek was not on the opening night roster, but injuries forced a quick call-up that turned into a success story. He played 17 games and looked like a player ready to stay, even if his point total was low with just one goal and two assists. His on-ice impact was promising for a 20-year-old defenseman, and his 51.58 expected Goals-For percentage at 5-on-5 was a solid mark. He has earned another look should the Blues need someone to fill the backend again. The team now has depth that was missing just a month ago. The Blues are 10-9-2 through 21 games, and three players are contributing in unexpected ways.

item.title: 49ers' Mike Evans ‘going in the right direction,' questionable to play vs. Vikings
item.description: San Francisco wide receiver Mike Evans celebrates a first down during the game between the 49ers and Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground stadium in Australia on Friday, Sept. 11, 2026. (Sydney Low/For the S.F. Chronicle) San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) practiced Thursday for the first time since he left the 49ers' Oct. 19 win over the Washington Commanders. On Friday, asked how Evans felt coming out of it, head coach Kyle Shanahan said he was "a little sore" but "going in the right direction." Evans was listed Thursday as a limited participant, and took part in individual drills during the open viewing portion of practice. He ran routes and caught passes at less than full speed. Shanahan said Evans will again be limited Friday during the 49ers' third practice at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado. "We're all half-speed," Shanahan said, "so we'll keep him out of one period, and then he'll be limited in the rest." San Francisco will make a decision on Evans' game status "probably tomorrow," according to Shanahan, depending on how he feels coming out of Friday's half-speed practice. The 49ers will have a final walkthrough Saturday morning before they fly to Mexico City for their Sunday night matchup against the Minnesota Vikings. General manager John Lynch said Thursday that the 49ers are being "extremely mindful" of the 33-year-old's long-term availability, and that he has "a chance" to play Sunday. "We're going to do what's in Mike's best interest so that when he's here, we can keep him out there," Lynch said on KNBR. "At least have the best chance of doing that." If Evans does play, he'll no longer be the 49ers' oldest wideout. Trade deadline acquisition Keenan Allen (34) would run routes alongside Evans and tight end George Kittle (33), making for an ultra-experienced and tall primary receiving group for quarterback Brock Purdy . Evans is 6-foot-5, Allen is 6-foot-2 and Kittle is 6-foot-4. "It's always good to have tall guys, but that only matters if they have really good hands," Shanahan said. "Fortunately, that's not the case with Mike and … Keenan." More injury notes: Cornerback Renardo Green (back) came off the injury report Friday after being a full participant at Thursday's practice. Green exited the 49ers' last two games early, and he was questionable entering last Sunday's contest against the Dallas Cowboys, but he has no injury designation this week. On Monday, Shanahan said he believed Green was just dealing with back tightness. San Francisco's other starting cornerback, Deommodore Lenoir, was a full participant all week after being limited last week by a foot issue. Lenoir, who played through the injury Sunday against Dallas, allowed 10 catches for 134 yards and three touchdowns on 17 targets. item.title: Charles Leclerc recalls getting stopped by Las Vegas club security as a teenager
item.description: Motorsport photo Today, Charles Leclerc can headline his own pop-up café at Wynn Las Vegas without waiting in line. Funnily enough, however, back when he first set foot in Nevada, he could not even make it past a nightclub bouncer. Appearing on The Fast And The Curious podcast during 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix week, the Ferrari driver opened up about why Sin City holds a personal place in his memory - including an awkward underage run-in with security long before Formula 1 arrived on the Strip. "Las Vegas was the first place I ever went to in the United States with my father back then," Leclerc recalled, referencing a major karting weekend in the city. "I was maybe 15 or 16, and I remember trying to go into a club for the very first time, and I got stopped by security, and my father had to come and pick me up at the security, which [was] quite embarrassing, but it's a funny memory now." The trip dates back to November 2012 - barely a month after Leclerc’s 15th birthday - when he competed in the SKUSA SuperNationals XVI on a temporary circuit at the Rio Hotel & Casino. Even if his nightlife debut ended at the door, his on-track performance stood out: he qualified on pole position in the TaG Senior class and finished fourth in the final. Read Also: Fan voting opens for the Autosport Awards Leclerc later returned to Las Vegas on vacation with close friends around 2017 or 2018, and laughed when hosts Betty Glover and Christian Hewgill asked if bouncers still gave him trouble. "I do now, I do, yeah. I'm over 21, so I'm all good now," Leclerc joked. He then paused to ask whether newly crowned 2026 World Champion Kimi Antonelli had turned 21 yet, only to realise the 20-year-old Mercedes driver is still barred from Vegas clubs himself. From karting memories to cold-weather challenges Since Formula 1 added the Las Vegas Strip Circuit to the calendar in 2023, the venue has been kind to Leclerc. He took pole position and finished runner-up to Max Verstappen in the inaugural race, followed by back-to-back fourth-place finishes in 2024 and 2025. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari "I love city tracks, and by definition I also really enjoy Las Vegas, but it's a particular track because it has such low grip and also the temperatures are so low that it has its own challenges," Leclerc said. On the podcast, he warned that cold conditions remain one of Ferrari’s biggest weaknesses in 2026. Even so, Leclerc made an encouraging start in Thursday night’s rain-hit second practice, clocking third fastest behind Mercedes’ George Russell and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly as Ferrari tries to keep its late-season momentum alive. item.title: Hafley Names Kenneth Grant As Next Startership After Phillips Injury
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Head coach Jeff Hafley has decided to hand the starting defensive tackle role to Kenneth Grant. This move comes after the team lost Jordan Phillips to a season-ending injury during the week. The decision was made public on Wednesday as the Dolphins prepare for a tough matchup. According to Dolphins Talk , Hafley stated clearly that Grant will immediately be relied upon for a significantly higher number of snaps. The Dolphins face a massive hole in their defensive line after losing three players in a short time. Zach Sieler is already out for the year, and now Phillips and Zeek Biggers are gone too. Phillips is undergoing surgery and both he and Biggers will go on injured reserve. The team must find a way to stop the run without these key veterans. Hafley praised the toughness of the players who are gone but said the team has no time to dwell on the bad luck. Grant Gets The Call Hafley did not hesitate when asked about who would fill the void left by Phillips. He pointed directly to the young talent in the locker room who is ready to step up. “It’s going to be KG’s turn,” Hafley said, using the rookie’s nickname to show his confidence. Grant has been working hard in practice and the coaching staff wants to see what he can do against a top-tier offense. The coach also noted that Keith Cooper Jr. would see more time after joining from the practice squad. Cooper has shown he can handle the speed of the NFL quickly. The new players have to learn the scheme fast because they will play on every down. Defensive line coach Austin Clark is calling these extra meetings “night school” to help them study. They need to understand first, second, and third-down calls plus red zone duties. Hafley gave credit to the group for putting in the extra work to get ready. The defense cannot simplify too much or the offense will exploit them for big gains. Brooks Still Elite Even with the losses up front, the linebacker unit is still performing at a high level. Jordyn Brooks has been a standout player despite the team struggling to win games. Hafley believes Brooks is playing at an elite level that should get him more national attention. “He’s playing at an All-Pro level,” Hafley said, backing up his claim with the player’s consistent play. Brooks has shown he can handle the pressure of a losing season and keep improving his game. The Dolphins will face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium. Hafley expects the new defensive linemen to step up and make plays for the defense. The coach also mentioned that Kyle McCord has another week of practice to get better before the big game. “I’d expect him to play better,” Hafley said, looking for growth from his young quarterback. The team will see if these changes work when they take the field on Sunday.

item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The DP World Tour has opened its gates for LIV Golf players to join in 2027. This move includes stars like Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, and Joaquin Niemann. Current members worry there will be no room left for them in the fields. The tour can fix this fear by copying the smart play the PGA Tour made with Brooks Koepka this year. When Koepka returned from LIV, the PGA Tour did not take a spot from a regular member. Instead, they added three extra spots to every event where Koepka played. This simple change kept the peace while letting a star compete. The DP World Tour needs to do the same thing next season to avoid angering its own roster. The Koepka Precedent for Field Size The PGA Tour faced a similar problem when Brooks Koepka decided to come back from the rival league. Tour officials knew that just letting him in could upset the players who stayed loyal. They needed a way to let him play without kicking anyone else out of the lineup. The solution was to grow the field size whenever he showed up. In 2026, whenever Koepka joined a field, three additional spots were created for other competitors. Consequently, his participation did not displace any PGA Tour member from an event. His presence genuinely expanded competitive chances for other players. Current members now worry about insufficient field space, and the situation has intensified this concern. The fear is real because tournament fields have a hard cap on how many players can enter. item.title: Giancarlo Stanton Causing Yankees Major Lineup Problem
item.description: New York Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton On Nov. 10, general manager Brian Cashman revealed that Giancarlo Stanton would be back with the New York Yankees in spring training, saying, "He's not going anywhere." While the Yankees expect Stanton back, his return is actually causing quite a few problems. Stanton cannot play in the field, meaning he is locked into the designated hitter spot. That is causing problems for Luis García Jr. and Aaron Judge. Last season, Stanton missed most of the year, and García played first base and Ben Rice played designated hitter. With Stanton back, Rice will go back to first base, meaning García will have to go back to playing second base, as he did for his entire career before last season. It would be really easy for the Yankees to just plug García in at second base if it were not for Anthony Volpe. Volpe looked good after his return from being demoted, and he figures to be part of the equation at second base. Ultimately, Stanton's return to the team has a ripple effect that essentially takes at-bats away from García. The only way around it is seemingly moving on from Volpe and giving García the keys to second base. Another option would be to move Volpe to third base full-time and move on from Ryan McMahon. However, as long as McMahon is on the team, the Yankees cannot commit to that plan. However, even if the Yankees were to do that, it's not really an upgrade at third base unless Volpe proves he can actually be a consistent offensive force. Going into the year, having to rely on that is not great. On top of all of that, the Yankees are reportedly exploring the third base market. If they do add an external third baseman to replace McMahon, then they are really in a bind with García's playing time. The easiest solution for the Yankees would be to move on from Stanton, play Rice at designated hitter, play García at first base, play Volpe at second base and then add a real upgrade at third base. Another ramification of Stanton's return is Aaron Judge's health. He missed most of last season, and he is not getting any younger. The Yankees may prefer to get him off his feet to help keep him healthy, but they cannot do that with Stanton clogging the designated hitter spot. item.description: Harry Kane was subbed out early with injury as his Bayern Munich side drew 1-1 at home with lowly Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday. El Mala had an excellent late chance to snare a first Cologne win at Bayern since 2009 but he pulled the ball just wide with the goal beckoning. Now a point behind Bayern, chasers Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first on the table if they win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury in yet another injury blow for the undermanned side. Bayern welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back after a month-long absence and midfielder Jamal Musiala after two months out on Friday, but are already without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer. Despite the draw Bayern, who play away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, remain the only undefeated side in Europe's top-five leagues in all competitions this season. Kompany returned to the dugout with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on the training pitch before being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October. Cologne, who arrived in Munich with just one league victory this season, took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent counter-attack. Moore pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala. With Bayern's defence closing in, El Mala stroked a no-look backheel in Moore's path and the Spurs loanee coolly rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and slid the ball home. Bayern went on the attack immediately but suffered another setback when Kane was brought down in the Cologne box from behind by defender Joel Schmied. Having his penalty appeals waved away, Kane rose gingerly and tried to continue, but was visibly limping and was subbed out soon after. With Cologne sitting deep, Bayern attacked from a distance and broke through before the break when Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom right to level the scores. The hosts suffered another blow in the dying stages of the opening half when Olise went down under a challenge. The France winger did not return to the field after half-time and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches. Sensing a first victory over Bayern since 2011 -- a run of 23 games including 21 defeats -- Cologne continued to push, with El Mala and Maina forcing a spectacular double save from Urbig just before the hour mark. item.title: David Law Slams LIV Invites: ‘Doesn’t Sit Right’
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images David Law isn’t buying the idea that special invites fix the European Tour. The 35-year-old Scot says handing out spots to former LIV Golf stars without them earning their way through Q-School feels wrong. He told GolfMagic that the beauty of the game lies in earning every single thing a player gets. This is grumbling and a direct challenge to the new membership rules confirmed for the 2027 season. Nine former LIV players are set to receive tournament invitations after striking deals with the circuit. Names like Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith, and Bubba Watson are on that list. Joaquin Niemann and Abraham Ancer are also included. The tour says these moves bring huge names back to Europe. Law admits that stars like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton add value by playing full time. But he draws a hard line at the players who skip the usual grind to get in. The Earning of a Spot Securing playing privileges on the European circuit is a struggle Law understands well. He has felt the pressure of the qualifying school himself. “Giving players a large number of invites when they haven’t gone through Q-School to earn their way onto our Tour doesn’t quite sit right with me,” Law said to GolfMagic. That quote hits the core of the issue. It is about the path they took rather than just hating big names. Bypassing the hard work of Q-School sets a bad example for the kids trying to make it the old-fashioned way. Some might argue that the tour needs star power to survive. Maybe it does. But the method of getting those stars matters. The DP World Tour confirmed these arrangements just a week before Law spoke up. The list includes legends like Sergio Garcia and Lee Westwood, who returned through the career-money category. That feels different than a free pass. The distinction is clear to Law, even if the tour office sees it differently. Slow Play Fines Loom While the LIV debate rages, another rule change is stirring up trouble for the LPGA Tour. Carlota Ciganda knows she is one of the slowest players on the circuit. On Thursday, she posted a 68 to open the CME Group Tour Championship and discussed the new policy. Starting next year, players timed on 35 holes will face a $35,000 fine. That number increases if the problem gets worse. “Obviously, being one of the slowest players, it’s not going to help me,” Ciganda told reporters. She thinks the fine might not even make that much of a difference in how fast rounds go. Lindy Duncan, a recent winner on the tour, sees the waste of time in waiting. “When you’re just standing there waiting, and the fans are just standing there, waiting, it feels like a waste of time,” Duncan said. The LPGA Tour has been strict on this before. While vying for the lead earlier this season, Ciganda was assessed a two-stroke penalty at the Buick Shanghai Invitational. The new financial penalty is a steep jump from the $5,000 fines players saw this year. Ciganda says she will try to play quicker to avoid paying that money.

item.title: Mets Reportedly Make Nearly $400m Offer to Tarik Skubal
item.description: The New York Mets offered Los Angeles Dodgers free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year, $390 million deal, which would shatter the previous record for largest contract for a pitcher. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) The current holder for largest contract ever for a pitcher is Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who will earn $325 million across his 10-year deal. New York’s massive offer to Skubal isn’t any surprise, as Jon Heyman of the New York post reported they were ready to go “all in” for the left-hander this offseason and said his meeting with them “went very well.” Does Tarik Skubal Deserve a Contract That Large? Skubal, despite missing some time while dealing with loose bodies in his elbow, had a fantastic 2026 season with the Detroit Tigers and the Dodgers, still managing to make 26 appearances on the mound despite his fairly serious injury. He totaled 158.2 innings between the Dodgers and Tigers, striking out 186 batters with a 2.72 ERA during that stretch. As far as left-handed pitchers in MLB go, Skubal is clearly one of the best in the game, and his last two healthy seasons reflect that. He led the American League in ERA in both the 2024 and 2025 seasons with marks below 2.40, and earned the AL Cy Young award in both. At 30 years old, Skubal still has a long career ahead of him in MLB. Oct 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) reacts during the fifth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game one of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Will the Dodgers Match That Figure? The Dodgers reportedly wanted to avoid long-term deals for Skubal as they did with Kyle Tucker last offseason, but Heyman reported they could break that trend for a talent like Skubal. “The Dodgers also have told folks there are circumstances whereby they’d still do longer deals, and they did them for Mookie Betts, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Shohei Ohtani in the past,” Heyman wrote. “To be a serious player, they’d almost have to go long considering the game’s best pitcher is extremely unlikely to have to settle for a short deal.” The Mets set the baseline with their offer, but there’s still plenty of negotiating to be done this offseason. With an official bid reported and less than two weeks before the MLB lockout, teams in contention for Skubal will be scrambling to top the contract.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
